name: vignette-bill-of-materials
scope: The D1b street vignette only, per game-design/decision-D1b-rescope.md. Not a district, not the town.
companion: production/specs/vignette-bill-of-materials.md is the reading copy. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE for every count quoted there.

route_values.HAVE: the bytes are in this repository now, licensed and attributed
route_values.FETCH: a free allowlisted library is the candidate route; see certainty
route_values.GENERATE: no library route; made here. See make_by for by what
route_values.BLOCKED: needs a decision from Jafar (a purchase, an account, a hardware buy)
route_values.ENGINE: not an asset at all; a renderer feature. Counted separately, never inside the asset denominator

make_by_values.PROC: composed from primitives by the scene generator from the shared JSON. No tool needed beyond the generator D1b requires anyway. Zero cost.
make_by_values.2D: the local image generator (stable-diffusion.cpp + Z-Image-Turbo, Apache-2.0, Vulkan) which already ran on Jafar's AMD machine and produced content/../Decals/generated. Zero cost, no account.
make_by_values.MESH3D: needs image-to-3D geometry synthesis. THIS is the capability blocked by the AMD card. Count these to size the blocker.

certainty_values.HELD: the bytes are on disk in this repo and were measured or listed this session
certainty_values.PROVEN-ROUTE: this exact fetch pattern has run for this project before and banked files
certainty_values.NEEDS-CHECKING: plausible, nobody has looked. Not an assertion about any library's contents

priority_values.MANDATORY: the camera cannot shoot the D1b scene without it
priority_values.DRESSING: the scene works without it and looks unfinished without it
priority_values.IF-IN-FRAME: only exists if the named shot condition holds

cameras_proposed.framing: eye height about 1.6 m on the pavement, looking along the street, kerb line running to the vanishing point
from the far kerb, square to the frontage, roofline in frame

groups.A: The ground from the camera to the vanishing point
groups.B: The edge where road meets pavement
groups.D: The upper facade and the skyline
groups.E: The furniture standing on the pavement
groups.F: Who and what is in the street
groups.G: The layer of dirt and paper over everything

items.what: The carriageway and footway themselves: two ground planes at different levels, with road camber falling to the gutter
items.source: scene generator from the shared JSON street path and widths
items.gate: generator placement count plus a datum check (does the ground exist under every footprint)
items.note: Added on review. A1 and A3 are the MATERIALS; nothing named the geometry they sit on. Camber matters more than it sounds under both D1b conditions: the fall to the gutter is what decides where A9's water collects, so a flat carriageway makes the wet frames wrong in a way no texture can fix.

items.what: Road surface material, colour plus normal plus roughness
items.note: Three maps only. Whether this id publishes AO and displacement is unchecked.

items.what: The AO and displacement maps the original fetch did not take, and 4K where published
items.source: ambientCG Asphalt012, same get?file= pattern the repo already uses
items.note: Quality ladder line, not a blocker. This is the one-field-away case the standing order names.

items.what: Pavement paving material
items.note: Whether the slab module reads as a British 900x600 concrete flag needs an eye check. Not re-sourced on suspicion.

items.what: Tarmac repair patch over slabs, the commonest British pavement fault
items.source: ambientCG asphalt or repair family, id unknown
items.note: Falls back to a 2D generated patch decal if no set exists.

items.what: Double yellow line pair running the length of the kerb
items.source: decal generator; check the six held RoadLines sets first, they are generic worn white paint
items.dims: two 100 mm bands, gap 100 mm, emitted along the kerb path from JSON
items.note: art-direction R-B4 names this among the highest value per polygon Britishness markers. Two yellow strips.

items.what: Worn white road markings, centre line and stop line
Road gully grate at the kerb
items.dims: measured 0.40 x 0.40 x 0.01 m, LOD0/1/2, 504 tris
items.gate: meshgen manifest (measured dims, sha256, licence block)

items.what: Manhole or inspection cover in the carriageway
items.source: decal ManholeCover011 (2K, with metalness) plus mesh drain_cover_01
items.licence: CC0-1.0, ambientCG and The Base Mesh
items.note: MEASURED FINDING: 0.10 m across is an inspection cover, not a manhole (a road manhole is 0.45 to 0.60 m). Use the decal on the road plane; do not rescale the mesh, the dims policy forbids inventing a number.

items.what: Mask saying where standing water sits, so the wet condition is not a uniformly wet plane
items.source: local image generator, or a procedural noise mask driven by the road's own low points
items.dims: tiling mask, resolution set at generation
items.gate: decal-ink.py blank check (the generator's known Vulkan blank-PNG failure is already instrumented)
items.note: NOT PREVIOUSLY LISTED ANYWHERE. Wet is a shader response plus a map of where the water is. A uniformly wet road reads as plastic and both D1b conditions are wet.

items.what: Kerbstone surface material
items.note: A material named kerb exists. The kerb GEOMETRY does not: see B1.

items.what: The kerb itself, an extruded profile following the road edge, with the upstand height that makes a pavement read as a pavement
items.source: scene generator from the shared JSON road path
items.dims: profile from the JSON, no invented model dims
items.gate: the generator's own placement count, plus a foot-gap style datum check per .claude/rules/instruments.md
items.note: Nothing among the 37 held props is a kerb. Whether Poly Haven's model library holds a British kerbstone is UNCHECKED, and it would be the wrong route anyway: the kerb follows a path that comes from JSON, so it must be emitted, not placed.

items.what: Dropped kerb at a vehicle crossover or crossing
items.source: same generator, a parameter of B1
items.condition: only if the shot includes a crossing or a yard entrance

items.what: The recess in the kerb line the gully grate sits in
items.note: A grate lying flat on an unbroken kerb line reads as a sticker.

items.what: Water running in the gutter, a decal strip
The building masses themselves, a run of terrace with shop at ground floor and flat above
items.source: scene generator from the shared JSON
items.gate: generator placement count plus paired stills
items.note: The repo holds Kenney city-kit buildings, CC0 and free, but they are flat-colormap low-poly with a hand-modelled silhouette, which is off the D8 photoreal bar. Held, not used. D1b's admissibility rule requires generator emission from JSON in any case.

items.what: Red or orange brick, the northern terrace surface
Blackened or grey brick, the hundred-years-of-pollution read
items.source: CityPack brick_grey (Bricks023), brick_grey_b (Bricks102), plus the generated wall_soot_brick.png overlay
items.licence: CC0-1.0 ambientCG; the overlay is generated here

items.what: Pebbledash or roughcast render, named in art-direction as the late-20th-century British facade
items.source: ambientCG, family unknown. Plaster001 and Plaster002 are held as a smooth-render fallback
items.note: I have not looked at ambientCG's catalogue for a pebbledash set and will not claim one exists.

items.what: Stallriser, pilasters, fascia band, transom, the four parts that make a British shopfront read as one
items.note: This is the single densest piece of Britishness at eye level and it is geometry, not a texture.

items.what: Shop name lettering on the fascia band
items.licence: generated by stable-diffusion.cpp with Z-Image-Turbo, Apache-2.0 weights, outputs unrestricted
items.gate: canon-gate.py, decal-ink.py, and the manifest's own review flag
items.note: The generated manifest marks every one review=pending: nothing ships until a human has looked for anything resembling a real mark. That look is an open action, not a done one.

items.what: Shop window glass and its reflection response
items.note: Both held ids are whole-facade photographs. Binding a facade photo to a single pane is a scale mismatch and needs an eye check before it is trusted.

items.what: Shop door, glazed upper half
Side door to the flat above, panelled, with a number and a letterplate
Closed roller shutter over a shopfront, which is what a British parade looks like at night
items.source: ambientCG CorrugatedSteel family, named in game-design/visual-bar-sources.md as page-confirmed but never fetched
items.note: Mandatory because the night condition needs at least one shut unit, and an open lit shopfront at 2am is the wrong picture. Geometry is PROC; only the surface is fetched.

items.what: What is visible through a lit window at night: a back-wall card with shelves, a bar, a stair
items.dims: card sized to the opening from JSON
items.note: NOT PREVIOUSLY LISTED. A lit window with nothing behind it is a glowing rectangle, and the night frame is half the D1b evidence.

items.what: Net curtain or blind in the flat window
items.source: local image generator or a plain translucent plane

items.what: Sills, lintels, thresholds, air bricks: the small reveals that stop a wall reading as a plane
Salt bloom and soot overlays for the wall surfaces
Roof covering, Welsh slate dark grey to black per art-direction
items.note: Held sets are roofing tiles by id. Whether either reads as slate rather than clay pantile needs an eye check; a red pantile roof on a northern terrace is a period and region error, not a taste one.

items.what: Brick chimney stack rising from the party wall
items.source: scene generator, brick material from C2/C3

items.what: Chimney pots on the stack
items.dims: measured 0.67 x 0.67 x 1.00 m and 0.95 x 0.95 x 0.67 m

items.what: Television aerial on the stack, the skyline marker of the era
items.source: scene generator, thin rods on a mast
items.note: visual-bar-sources.md records it as not CC0-fetchable anywhere and recommends procedural. Agreed: it is a comb of cylinders.

items.what: Rainwater downpipe with hopper and shoe, the British vertical
items.note: art-direction names drainpipes as the British answer to the American fire escape. Also the anchor for the Leaking005 stain decal already held.

items.what: Eaves gutter and fascia board
Parapet and coping where the frontage is flat-topped
Sash windows to the flat above, with reveal depth
items.note: Reveal depth is the cheap facade-rhythm win named in the M17.10 decomposition. A window flush with the wall reads as a decal.

items.what: Street lighting column, swan neck, at a height that lights a carriageway
items.note: MEASURED FINDING: the held lamp_post_01 measures 0.37 x 0.27 x 3.00 m. Three metres is amenity or park height; a British residential lighting column of the period is roughly 5 to 6 m. The lantern height decides the whole night image (throw, shadow length, how much of the frame is lit), so this is the highest-consequence measurement in the document. Rescaling the held mesh is forbidden by the dims policy; emitting a column at a height named in JSON is not.

items.what: The lantern itself, the bowl on the swan neck, with an emissive surface
items.note: Colour is physics, not taste: low pressure sodium is monochromatic at 589 nm with colour rendering index 0, sourced in art-direction R-B3. Geometry here; the light itself is H4.

items.what: Red telephone kiosk
items.source: scene generator, a glazed box with a crown-less pediment
items.note: Two facts, both binding. visual-bar-sources.md records no CC0-fetchable kiosk anywhere. And canon requires every brand fictional: the kiosk silhouette is architecture and fine, but the lettering and the crown are real marks and must be replaced with a Meridian operator invented in the brand bible. Nobody has written that brand.

items.what: Red pillar box
items.source: scene generator, a cylinder with a cap and a slot
items.note: Same brand rule as E3: the cypher and any lettering must be fictional. art-direction R-B4 counts the red boxes as the entire high-chroma accent budget of a British street, so this and E3 carry the colour of the frame between them.

items.what: Pavement bollards
Public litter bins
Benches
items.condition: a bench belongs on a wide pavement or a quay, not on a narrow parade

items.what: Pedestrian guard railing at the kerb
items.note: The held trunk_protection_railing (2.06 x 2.04 x 0.60 m) is a tree pit guard, not a kerb rail. Different object, and calling it one would be the kind of substitution this document exists to prevent.

items.what: Victorian tree pit guard
items.condition: only if a street tree is in the scene, and no tree is on this list

items.what: Street name plate on the wall or on a post, carrying a canon street name
items.source: local image generator or a text-plate decal; plate geometry is PROC
items.note: canon mints Quay Street, Weighhouse Lane and Tannery Row. A street with no name plate is a set; a street with a canon name is Meridian.

items.what: Traffic cones and a crowd barrier
items.dims: measured 0.45, 0.45 m tall and 2.29 x 0.40 x 1.14 m

items.what: Pavement A-board and wall-mounted poster frames
items.note: The carrier is held; what it carries is G6.

items.what: Galvanised metal household dustbin, the pre-wheelie British bin
items.source: scene generator, a ribbed cylinder and a lid
items.note: art-direction names wheelie-less metal dustbins specifically. None of the four held bins is one: they are all public street bins.

items.what: Crates, pallets, barrels and a builder's skip
items.source: wooden_crate_01/02, pallet, small_pallet, large_pallet, oil_barrel, wood_barrel, skip
items.note: Strongly on brief for a port town and already measured. The cheapest density in the document.

items.what: Belisha beacon at a crossing, black and white pole with a yellow globe
items.condition: only if the scene includes a pedestrian crossing
items.note: The second of the two mandated high-chroma accents art-direction R-B4 names.

items.what: Parking meter
items.condition: only on a metered frontage; recorded as not CC0-fetchable in visual-bar-sources.md

items.what: Bus shelter
items.condition: only if a stop is in frame; recorded as not CC0-fetchable in visual-bar-sources.md

items.what: Retractable shop awning over a frontage
items.note: awning_01 carries 20 triangles and one LOD rung; awning_02 carries 644 and three. Use awning_02. Both were named by no line of this list until this correction.

items.what: Direction finger post
items.condition: only at a junction or a quayside where a direction sign belongs; a finger post mid-parade is wrong
items.note: _01 is 0.50 m tall and 32 triangles: a blade for an existing post, not a post. _03 is the only one with a full LOD chain.

items.what: One clothed character body, which D1b names as mandatory scene content
items.licence: Mixamo, on Jafar's account, allowlisted under Characters
items.dims: not measured this session; tools/body-proportions.py exists and should print the series before one is picked
items.note: Sufficient for admissibility, open on quality. These are game-resolution bodies in contemporary casual dress against a photoreal bar, and the period is 1988 to 1992. See F2.

items.what: Clothing that reads as 1988 to 1992 Britain rather than contemporary casual
items.source: no free re-dress route exists for a Mixamo body. Allowlist offers MetaHuman (free under 1M revenue) and Character Creator 4 exports, each a pipeline rather than an asset
items.licence: allowlisted either way; no purchase involved for MetaHuman under the threshold
items.note: BLOCKED means it needs a decision, and the decision is Jafar's about where the character pipeline goes, not about money. RECOMMENDATION: do not block D1b on it. D1b measures the pipeline, not the wardrobe; take a held body for the probe and put period wardrobe on the quality ladder with a name.

items.what: One idle or standing animation so the body is not a T-pose in the still
items.source: ledger/Assets/Characters/{A,B,C,D}/*.fbx, 64 clips accepted plus 7 marked rejected
items.note: A T-posed body in the still has happened in this project before and passed every numeric gate.

items.what: One parked period British car, boxy hatchback or estate
items.source: held vehicles exist (Kenney car-kit 50 files, OGA vehicles 31) but are flat-colormap low-poly and several are American types. Whether any CC0 library holds a photoreal-grade period British car is unchecked
items.licence: CC0-1.0 for what is held; unknown for any new fetch
items.condition: only if the shot list puts a car at the kerb
items.note: Largest quality risk on the list if included. The vignette can be shot without a vehicle and probably should be for the first pair. canon also forbids real car models, so a recognisable real shape is a canon violation as well as a bar risk.

items.what: Water and leak staining below hoppers, sills and gutters
items.source: Decals/ambientcg/Leaking005, 2K PNG with opacity and roughness
items.note: Mandatory because surface history is one of the four parts of the kept M17.10 decomposition and this is its cheapest instance.

items.what: Potholes, patches and road scars
Dirt, wear and scratch masks for breaking up flat surfaces
Damp growth at wall feet and in joints
Stickers and torn paper remains on posts and boxes
Fly-posted gig bills and public notices, period-fictional
items.licence: generated here, Apache-2.0 weights, outputs unrestricted
items.note: Also review=pending in the generated manifest.

items.what: Marker and chrome tags of the period, naming in-world crews
items.note: visual-bar-sources.md recorded graffiti as a GAP with no CC0 source found. That was 21 August, before the local image generator ran on this hardware. The gap is closed by a capability the research could not know about, at zero cost.

items.what: Chip papers, cans, cigarette ends in the gutter and against the wall feet
items.source: scene generator, flat cards and small primitives, scattered from JSON
items.note: NOT PREVIOUSLY LISTED. A clean gutter in 1990 Britain is the tell that a street was built rather than lived in.

items.what: Trodden gum spots on the pavement
items.source: decal generator, a dark ellipse at high roughness
items.note: visual-bar-sources.md says explicitly: gap, do not source, one line of decal generator. Agreed and carried forward.

items.what: Overcast daylight environment, which art-direction R-B2 makes the DEFAULT frame rather than a side case
items.note: 2K is the fetched rung. Poly Haven publishes higher rungs for most HDRIs and a sky fills a large fraction of an outdoor frame, so this is a named quality ladder item: re-fetch at 4K by changing one path segment. Whether this specific slug publishes 4K is unchecked.

items.what: Overcast night environment with distant urban glow
items.note: Same 2K ladder note as H1. Two further HDRIs are held (industrial_sunset_puresky, misty_farm_road) and neither condition D1b names needs them.

items.what: The directional light and its elevation, capped at 59 degrees at noon by latitude
items.source: each engine's own sun, driven from the scene JSON date and time
items.note: Not an asset and it still decides the frame. art-direction R-B1 gives the number from arithmetic: a Los Santos noon sun is the fastest way to make a British street read as somewhere else.

items.what: The practical lights themselves at night: the sodium lamp emitters
items.source: each engine's point or spot lights, placed by the generator at the lantern positions from JSON
items.note: D1b names practical lights at night as mandatory content. The geometry is E1 and E2; this row is the light. Colour is fixed by physics (589 nm, CRI 0) and the count is set by the column spacing in the JSON, so the two must be emitted together or the lamps glow with nothing lit under them.

items.what: Light spilling from lit shopfronts and flats onto the wet pavement
items.note: The second light source of the night frame and the one that makes a wet pavement worth having.

items.what: The wet BRDF: darkened albedo, lowered roughness, reflection of everything above the ground
items.source: each engine's material and reflection path, driven by the A9 mask
items.note: art-direction R-B5 calls wet ground the Britishness multiplier and the cheapest depth cue there is. Both D1b conditions are wet, so this is the single feature the paired stills are most likely to be decided on, and it is where the two engines are most likely to differ.

items.what: Atmospheric depth: haze that separates the near frontage from the far end of the street
Falling rain, as particles or as a screen effect
items.condition: the D1b conditions are wet, not necessarily raining. Falling rain in a still is mostly invisible and costs an engine-specific system, so it is a deliberate maybe rather than a requirement.

not_on_this_list_deliberately.why: Era unverified. I do not know when blister tactile paving became normal on British streets and it may be after 1992. Check before placing; placing it on a guess would be a period error of the kind canon says is corrected on sight.

not_on_this_list_deliberately.what: Fire escapes, fire hydrants, stop signs, overhead wooden utility poles, wide setbacks, palm-scale street trees
not_on_this_list_deliberately.why: American tells, named as such in art-direction. The held Kenney kits contain several of them.
Era risk in the same class as tactile paving, and art-direction asks for the metal dustbin instead (E13).
No tree is on this list. The held tree pit railing (E9) implies one, so either both are in the scene or neither is.

not_on_this_list_deliberately.what: Anything from Meshy, Tripo, a cloud GPU or a Fab purchase
not_on_this_list_deliberately.why: Paid. No purchase is authorised and nothing on this list needs one.

not_on_this_list_deliberately.what: The whole town, the other six districts, interiors, water and the tidal edge
not_on_this_list_deliberately.why: Out of scope by the D1b re-scope ruling. A list of twenty things that can be acted on beats two thousand that cannot.

held_props_coverage.what: Of the 37 props already cleaned, measured and licence-tagged by the props-local-01 run, how many are named by a line of this list.
held_props_coverage.why_not: lamp_post_01 measures 3.00 m tall, which is amenity height rather than street lighting height. It appears in E1 as a MEASUREMENT and is deliberately not used as an asset. Recorded here rather than left silent, because a fetched prop no line names is the failure this project keeps finding.
